clue.text: Become tired, one needs the support of staff

definitions.meaning: to wilt or lose energy, as a runner does late in a race

definitions.text: one needs the support of staff
definitions.meaning: a banner is hoisted on a pole, its staff, which holds it up

explanation.surface: An exhausted worker leans on colleagues to get through the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as employees, but it is the pole a banner flies from.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop or weaken is the verb sense; the noun is a banner hung on a pole.

clue.text: Not quite satisfied about cheese write-up that's critical

indicators.note: about means going round, so the cut word encloses the cheese
not quite means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: full means satisfied after a meal

indicators.note: in a down clue a write-up is read upwards, so the cheese runs backwards

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A diner, not quite full, writes a critical review of the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write-up' looks like a restaurant review, but in a down clue it means the cheese is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive, momentous moment is a critical one, one with grave consequences.

clue.text: Sound of a lot of vowels, without a single consonant

parts.words: of a lot of vowels, without a single consonant
parts.note: describes the word itself: four of the five vowels and only one consonant among them

explanation.surface: Someone describes speech made of vowels with no consonants.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest after 'Sound' is a description of the word's letters, not a separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sound, as in recordings, the word is used to mean sound itself.

clue.text: Henry and Alfred having a little drink

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
Alf is the short form of the name Alfred

explanation.surface: Two friends, Henry and Alfred, share a small drink at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub a half is half a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-pint of beer is the smaller measure ordered in a British pub.

clue.text: A second-class grade

parts.note: a sort is a class or kind

explanation.surface: A student is given a second-class mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify or sort things into groups is to grade them.

clue.text: Barbed wire

parts.note: reads as fencing, but means a hooked metal piece on an angler's line

explanation.surface: A fence of spiked wire.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's barbed metal hook is a curved piece of wire with a barb.

clue.text: Sounds like foul gangster comes to premature end

definitions.note: the definition is a fowl, the bird word that sounds the same as foul

indicators.note: ending too soon means the gangster's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era

explanation.surface: Rumours of foul play surround a mobster's early death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' looks like an adjective about the gangster's deeds, but 'Sounds like foul' defines a fowl: a castrated cockerel.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a kind of poultry.

clue.text: During which rustics may enjoy bringing in hay?

definitions.text: During which rustics may enjoy bringing in hay?

parts.words: During which rustics may enjoy bringing in hay?
parts.note: the hay is not harvest but an old rural dance, so the activity is a folk dance

explanation.surface: Farmhands take pleasure in gathering the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: A hay (or hey) is an old English rural dance with interweaving lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk dancing of the English rural tradition, in which a hay is one figure.

clue.text: Fish with rod using wooden shaft

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: An angler catches a pike with a rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' only links the pieces to the definition; this shaft once carried a pike, the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden pole of a pike, the old infantry spear, is its shaft.

clue.text: Children delivered by forceps

definitions.meaning: pincers, a gripping tool like forceps

explanation.surface: Babies are delivered with forceps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered by' only links the two definitions; the surface is a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Kids are informally called by this British word, which also names a pincer tool.

clue.text: Sea, where river enters it, seen to be very agitated

definitions.meaning: read literally: sea spray at the estuary where a river flows into the sea
to be furious, frothing with rage

explanation.surface: A stormy sea churns where a river flows into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen to' only links; the first half is a literal picture of surf at an estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Frothing at the lips is the idiom for raging with fury.

clue.text: It's tiring working outside

indicators.note: working here means set in motion and rearranged, so the next word's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that outdoor labour is exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome and boring wears a person out, so it is tiring.

clue.text: High and, mighty robbed at gunpoint

definitions.meaning: haughty and snobbish, looking down on others
held up by an armed robber, as in a stick-up

explanation.surface: An arrogant grandee gets mugged by a gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'High and mighty' without the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooty people are haughty; a stick-up is an armed robbery, so its victim was held up.

clue.text: Demonstration by Frenchman how to move a resister

parts.note: Frog is an old British slang term for a Frenchman
a protest march is a demonstration

explanation.surface: A French protester's demonstration ends with police dragging resisters away.
explanation.walkthrough: To frogmarch someone is to force them forward with arms pinned behind, as police do with an unwilling arrestee. 'by' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names forcing an uncooperative person along with their arms held behind them.

clue.text: Experience a smack

definitions.meaning: to sample or undergo something, as in getting a first experience of fame
a smack is a slight flavour, as in a smack of garlic

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being slapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample or try something is one sense; a faint flavour or hint is the other.

clue.text: Gets down into the lungs

definitions.meaning: to alight is to get down, as from a horse or vehicle
the lungs of a slaughtered animal, sold as offal or pet food

explanation.surface: Someone inhales deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' only joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to descend from a vehicle; offal butchers call animal lungs by this name.

clue.text: Mediator providing information about zero risk to partners

indicators.note: about means around, so the information wraps round the rest

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
O looks like zero
a bet is a risk or wager
West and East are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: A negotiator gives news that partners face no risk.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, and West and East play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary who carries messages between two sides acts as a mediator.

clue.text: Children imitating apes, lion and' tiger, say

parts.note: to ape is to copy, imitate
lions and tigers are examples of big cats

explanation.surface: Kids at the zoo mimic monkeys and big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'and' is OCR noise; the scan prints 'lion and tiger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimics, especially youngsters who imitate others, are called by this playground term.

clue.text: Material to study on island

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the study comes first

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A student researches building material on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: A building material made of cement, sand and gravel.

clue.text: Small bonnet for American in infancy

parts.note: baby means small, as in baby carrots
the British car bonnet is the hood in the USA

explanation.surface: A tiny bonnet is bought for an American baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonnet' suggests a baby's hat, but it is the engine cover of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Babyhood is the earliest stage of life, the time of being an infant.

clue.text: Appear' comical in sleeping bag

parts.note: to be is to appear or exist, the bare verb
droll means comical

explanation.surface: Someone looks funny in a sleeping bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'Appear' is OCR noise; the scan shows a smudge, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding rolled up for carrying, used as a sleeping bag when camping.

clue.text: Don't start crying, getting severe rebuke

indicators.note: telling the word not to start means its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: tearful means crying

explanation.surface: A child is told not to cry after being scolded harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a scolding or long tirade is to get this, an idiom for a dressing-down.

clue.text: A bad spell on the shore, say

indicators.note: say means spoken aloud, so the shore word sounds like the answer

parts.note: littoral means of or on the seashore

explanation.surface: A bout of foul weather hits the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' suggests a period of weather, but it means spelling: a printer's misprint is called a literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers call a typo or misprint by this name; a misprint is a bad spelling.

clue.text: Person who shoots birds on river

parts.note: snipe are wading birds, the plural being the same

explanation.surface: A hunter shoots birds on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman firing from hiding is a sharpshooter.

clue.text: Information provided by corporation lawyer in US originally

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, the American public prosecutor
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, so tum

explanation.surface: Data comes from a company's American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company but means a paunch. 'provided by' and 'originally' only link; the DA order is lawyer first, belly after.
explanation.definitionFit: A single fact or given figure is the singular of data, a piece of information.

clue.text: Pressed' soldier to learn writing

definitions.note: a soldier pressed into service, forced to enlist

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
script means handwriting or written text

explanation.surface: A new recruit is made to study his letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'Pressed' is OCR noise; the scan prints no apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is compelled to serve, just as pressed men were forced into the navy.

clue.text: Liquor circulating in the gods

parts.note: in Greek myth the ethereal fluid that flows in divine veins instead of blood

explanation.surface: Drink is passed round in the theatre gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the gods' suggests the cheap top seats in a theatre, but means the Greek deities.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethereal fluid flowing in divine veins in Greek myth, their counterpart of blood.

clue.text: Breakable: oeuvre's getting too much handling

indicators.note: something breakable can be broken up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fragile body of artistic work is being handled too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive use or handling wears a thing out; the noun means use beyond what is wise.

clue.text: One of 8 who steals

definitions.meaning: 8 down's answer is a word for pincers, and each jaw of the pair nips
to pinch is British slang for to steal, so one who steals

explanation.surface: A thief is one of eight in a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' is a cross-reference to 8 down, the pair of pincers, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: One that nips or grips is one sense; a petty thief, from slang 'pinch', is the other.

clue.text: Food no one can eat freely

definitions.text: Food no one can eat freely

parts.words: Food no one can eat freely
parts.note: a nod to the saying that there is no such thing as a free midday meal

explanation.surface: Nobody gets to eat without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'there's no such thing as a free lunch' means everything has a hidden cost.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says no midday meal comes without cost, so this meal is one nobody gets for nothing.

clue.text: Make note on organ

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the short note follows the organ

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A musician writes a note on an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' wants to be a musical letter A to G; here it is n., the written abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to gain wages, a synonym for earning.

clue.text: Centre of immorality, so it's said

indicators.note: the centre of the word holds the run, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: Someone claims a place is the heart of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so it's' only joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, as in spoken evidence or a viva exam.
